cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Leave the director's name on the launch programme. The department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Put it in my drawer. Without her, they'll each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give them equal introductions; nobody inherits the microphone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 keeps the director symbol above department heads, A3 commands hidden resignation and A5 personally allocates speech and equal introductions, exercising status to preserve balance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 printed resignation threatens A1 programme; A3 hides it; B4 speech requests prompt A5 proxy reading and equal introductions. B4 absence knowledge does not imply heads know resignation.

relationship.evidence: B2 flags concrete contradictory evidence and B4 brings competing real requests; B is organizing an event under pressure.

heightening.evidence: B4 contested speech causes A5 to retain the absent director as nominal speaker while preventing any head from inheriting the microphone.

specificity.evidence: A1 launch hierarchy and B2 resignation state the destabilizing truth; A3 explicitly identifies rival claims as the reason to hide it.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 nobody inherits the microphone makes a physical speaking object carry the succession conflict, earned by B4 request.

coach2.stated: A1 programme names the director; B2 resignation is printing; A3 fears rival claims; B4 heads ask for speech; A5 reads on her behalf.
coach2.inferred: Heads may know the director is absent without knowing she resigned; no assumption that the concealment already succeeded is needed.
coach2.missing: No essential fact missing; exact director whereabouts are irrelevant to A strategy.
coach2.firstDefect: No material comprehension defect; knowledge of absence versus resignation remains a distinction.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 identifies evidence that contradicts A1 continued director listing.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 hides B2 evidence and explains the balance-of-power risk.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 gives a concrete speech allocation problem related to A3 rivalry.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 allocates B4 speech without promoting a competing head.
